- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., > -0.16 or 0.27), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, model often underestimates the decline; adjust downward by 3–7% for 2–4 days.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–7 day) reversals; apply a 2–5% downward bias to 1–7 day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overfit recent noise; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecasts and avoid overreaction to single-day sentiment shifts.
- For 14+ day forecasts, model often underestimates mean reversion; add 2–5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, especially if recent price is below 30-day average.
